close_reason: OnExists::Replace branch now consults on_destroy_remove_children. When true and descendants exist, the handler cascades destroy of all descendants (each added to destroyed_list), then destroys the colliding node, then proceeds to create. When false, the prior nodeHasChildren guard is preserved. Two new integration tests (filenode_set_create_replace_with_remove_children_cascades, filenode_set_create_replace_without_flag_returns_node_has_children) use MemoryBackend to exercise both paths end-to-end. Committed in 42d77e7. Gates: fmt/clippy/test/doc green.
description:
draft-ietf-jmap-filenode-13 §3.2.3 (lines 565-570): 'If "replace", the existing item will be destroyed. In this case, the server MUST include the id of the replaced item in the destroyed response list. NOTE: if the replaced item is a directory which has children, then the server MUST respond with a nodeHasChildren error to this action UNLESS onDestroyRemoveChildren is true.'

The current src/filenode.rs:245-306 (OnExists::Replace branch) checks get_descendant_ids on the existing node and returns nodeHasChildren whenever the descendant list is non-empty. It does NOT consult on_destroy_remove_children.

Trigger: client sends FileNode/set create with onExists='replace' AND onDestroyRemoveChildren=true, where the colliding sibling is a directory containing child nodes. Bad behavior: handler returns nodeHasChildren even though the spec requires the replace+cascade combination to succeed (destroying the existing directory and its descendants, then creating the new node).

Required: when on_destroy_remove_children is true, the OnExists::Replace path must cascade destroy of descendants first (same logic as the destroy branch at filenode.rs:624-675), include all destroyed ids in destroyed_list, then destroy the existing node, then create the new one.
title: onExists='replace' guard ignores onDestroyRemoveChildren when destroying replaced directory with children
